name: Caesar And Cleopatra
summary: Two-player influence contest over five patrician groups where players win patrons for victory points.
rules_text: Two players are Caesar (Romans) and Cleopatra (Egyptians). Five patrician groups with 3-5 patron cards each lie between them. Each player has 50 cards: 37 influence cards numbered 1-5 or P, and 13 action cards. They set aside two of each 1-5, place one of each 1-5 face-down one per group, keep the other five as starting hand, shuffle rest as influence deck and stack action cards in chosen order as action deck. Each gets a secret bonus card requiring 3 patrons of a named group for 2 VP. On a turn the active player may play one action card, then must play 1 face-down card to one group or 2 face-up cards to one or two groups, respecting max 5 per player per group and 8 total per group, then refills to 5 cards choosing deck per draw, then draws a vote token. Or player may be passive: discard up to 5 and refill, no vote draw. When a vote card is drawn or a group reaches 8 total cards, reveal face-down cards in that group, sum values; higher sum wins one patron card from the group, then winner discards her highest, loser discards his lowest from that group. When a group is empty, clear its influence. Game ends when patrons are gone; most VP from patrons plus group majorities, group sweeps and secret bonus wins.
rating_reason: Two-sided card struggle with influence, fits hidden hands and arithmetic ranking
